findings.issue_text: flusher.py:255 — `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False for spawn-context processes (`SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`), so a hung flusher process is never killed before a replacement is spawned; the hung process leaks and if it resumes, two processes flush the same shards concurrently producing duplicate segments to Kafka. Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`.

flusher.py:341 — In `join`, the `break` when `remaining_time <= 0` exits the loop before `terminate()` runs for remaining processes, so on deadline expiry every unvisited process is left running; drop the `break` and always fall through to terminate. The `terminate()` call also has the same `isinstance` problem and is a no-op for spawn processes.

test_flusher.py — No test exercises the restart path (`_ensure_processes_alive` with a dead or hung process) for the new multi-process layout, and no test verifies that shards sharing a process are all flushed when `flusher_processes < len(shards)`; `test_flusher_processes_limit` only checks bookkeeping counts and never submits a span.

test_consumer.py:62 — `time.sleep(0.1)` added to give flusher threads time is a no-op because the test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` earlier, so the intended flakiness fix does nothing and the comment is misleading.

flusher.py:57 — `max_processes` is not validated: `--flusher-processes 0` silently falls through to all shards, and a negative value makes `num_processes` negative so `i % num_processes` yields an index missing from `process_to_shards_map`, crashing with `KeyError` on startup. Reject values < 1.

flusher.py:199 — Metric tag key is `"shard"` for `flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` but `"shards"` for `flusher.wait_produce`, so the timers cannot be grouped by the same tag; `flusher_unhealthy` uses a per-shard integer while the others use a comma-joined string, a third shape for the same dimension.

flusher.py:31 — Docstring says "Creates one process per shard", but the implementation creates `min(max_processes, len(shards))` processes and the CLI default is 1, so production normally runs a single process handling all shards.
flusher.py:127 — `_create_process_for_shard` is never called anywhere; dead code that will drift from `_create_process_for_shards`.

flusher.py:246 — `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` is now enforced per process index rather than per flusher, so N flusher processes tolerate roughly N times as many crashes before restarting the consumer, and `flusher_unhealthy` is incremented once per shard so a single hang in a process owning K shards counts as K unhealthy events, silently changing alerting semantics.

goldens.comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_flusher.py — No test exercises the restart path (`_ensure_processes_alive` with a dead or hung process) for the new multi-process layout, and no test verifies that shards sharing a process are all flushed when `flusher_processes < len(shards)`; `test_flusher_processes_limit` only checks bookkeeping counts and never submits a span.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new logic in `SpanFlusher`: multi-process shard mapping (`process_to_shards_map`), per-process health/backpressure tracking, and restart behavior in `_ensure_processes_alive` that kills/recreates a specific process for its shard set. The new test `test_flusher_processes_limit` only asserts bookkeeping (`len(flusher.processes)`, `max_processes`, `num_processes`, and shard assignment counts) and then `step.join()`; it never submits any messages/spans nor validates that flushing works when multiple shards share a process. No test in the diff forces a process to be dead/hung to exercise `_ensure_processes_alive` restart behavior. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher.py:57 — `max_processes` is not validated: `--flusher-processes 0` silently falls through to all shards, and a negative value makes `num_processes` negative so `i % num_processes` yields an index missing from `process_to_shards_map`, crashing with `KeyError` on startup. Reject values < 1.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means `--flusher-processes 0` is treated as falsy and becomes `len(assigned_shards)`, silently ignoring the user-specified 0. Worse, a negative value is truthy, so `self.max_processes` becomes negative and `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` can be negative. That yields an empty `process_to_shards_map` (`range(self.num_processes)`), then `process_index = i % self.num_processes` produces indices that are not present, causing `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index]` to raise `KeyError` during startup. The new click option (`type=int`) does not validate positivity.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher.py:31 — Docstring says "Creates one process per shard", but the implementation creates `min(max_processes, len(shards))` processes and the CLI default is 1, so production normally runs a single process handling all shards.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher`’s docstring it states: “Creates one process per shard for parallel processing.” However, the implementation explicitly caps process count: `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, and then assigns shards round-robin to those processes via `process_to_shards_map`. Additionally, the consumer CLI wiring sets `--flusher-processes` default to `1` and passes it through `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` into `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`, so in typical production config this will create a single flusher process handling all assigned shards. This is a real, diff-grounded mismatch between documentation and behavior, but not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher.py:127 — `_create_process_for_shard` is never called anywhere; dead code that will drift from `_create_process_for_shards`.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher` a helper `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is added, but the diff shows no call sites for it. Restarts are handled in `_ensure_processes_alive()` via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, and initial startup uses `_create_processes()` -> `_create_process_for_shards(...)`. As written, `_create_process_for_shard` is dead code and could diverge from `_create_process_for_shards` over time; it should be removed or wired into a real shard-level restart path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher.py:246 — `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` is now enforced per process index rather than per flusher, so N flusher processes tolerate roughly N times as many crashes before restarting the consumer, and `flusher_unhealthy` is incremented once per shard so a single hang in a process owning K shards counts as K unhealthy events, silently changing alerting semantics.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in the diff: restart accounting changed from a single counter (`self.process_restarts`) to per-process counters (`self.process_restarts[process_index]`), and the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS check is now applied per process (see `_ensure_processes_alive`: `if self.process_restarts[process_index] > MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS: ...; self.process_restarts[process_index] += 1`). This means a flusher with N processes can experience ~N× more total crashes before the consumer is forced to restart. Also, `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` is now emitted once per shard in an unhealthy process (`for shard in shards: metrics.incr(..., tags={..., "shard": shard})`), whereas previously it was emitted once per flusher event, changing alerting/metrics semantics. These are real, diff-grounded behavioral/observability changes, but not a clear correctness defect on their own.
